svg.aria-label: Diagram: CloudWatch Logs offers two log group classes. Standard is a full-featured option for logs that require real-time monitoring or logs you access frequently. Essentials, formerly Infrequent Access, offers a subset of capabilities including managed ingestion, storage, cross-account log analytics and encryption with a lower ingestion price per GB, and is described as ideal for ad-hoc querying and after-the-fact forensic analysis on infrequently accessed logs. The economics are narrower than a storage tier: the documentation states that for charges the two classes differ in ingestion costs only, and that storage charges and CloudWatch Logs Insights charges are the same in each log class, so there is no storage discount and no retrieval penalty. What Essentials removes is the reading and watching apparatus. GetLogEvents and FilterLogEvents are not supported, and the documentation directs you to use CloudWatch Logs Insights instead, which is billed on data scanned under the DataScanned-Bytes usage type against StartQuery. Field indexing is not supported either, and the query language reflects that: log groups in the Essentials class support all query commands except pattern, diff, filterIndex and unmask. So every read is a billed scan and the documented way to reduce scan volume is unavailable. Metric filters and subscription filters are also unsupported, which closes the metric-filter route to alarming on logs and removes the option of streaming events out for your own processing, while Scheduled Queries are supported in both classes so a log alarm remains the surviving route, billed on the data it scans. Live Tail, Anomaly Detection, embedded metrics format, Container Insights and Lambda Insights log ingestion, Facets, natural language query assist and compare to previous time range are all Standard only. Both classes keep managed ingestion and storage, cross-account features, KMS encryption, discovered fields, pipeline transformation, export to Amazon S3, S3 Tables integration, scheduled queries, OpenSearch PPL and SQL querying, and sensitive data protection with masking. The class is permanent: after a log group is created its log class cannot be changed, so migration means a new log group and every reference to it. A third Delivery class exists only for delivering AWS Lambda logs to Amazon S3 or Amazon Data Firehose, where events are kept two days on a fixed retention that cannot be changed and Logs Insights queries are not offered. Finally the rename: both INFREQUENT_ACCESS and ESSENTIALS are accepted as input indefinitely, and starting December 2026 read-path API responses return ESSENTIALS, a name change only with no changes to functionality or pricing, so code comparing the old literal stops matching without erroring.
svg.title: The saving is at ingestion only, and the class cannot be changed afterwards
svg.text: It looks like a storage tier. It is a feature tier, priced at the door.
“For charges, the Standard and Essentials (formerly Infrequent Access) log classes differ in ingestion costs
only. Storage charges and CloudWatch Logs Insights charges are the same in each log class.”
BOTH CLASSES KEEP
Managed ingestion + storage · KMS encryption
Cross-account · masking · discovered fields
Export to S3 · S3 Tables · Pipeline transforms
Scheduled Queries — so a Log Alarm still works
Storage and query prices are identical either way.
ESSENTIALS GIVES UP
GetLogEvents FilterLogEvents field indexing
metric filters subscription filters Live Tail
anomaly detection EMF Container/Lambda Insights
facets query assist compare to previous range
Everything that watches a log as it arrives.
The two rows that interact badly
GetLogEvents / FilterLogEvents unsupported — “Use CloudWatch Logs Insights to view log events”.
Logs Insights is billed on data scanned. And field indexing is unsupported here too.
So every read is a billed scan, in the one class where no index can narrow it.
Query commands unsupported: pattern, diff, filterIndex, unmask.
Where #112 and #113 land
metric filter + metric alarm Standard only — this route closes
Log Alarm on scheduled query both classes — the surviving route
And its cost is the data it scans, with #113’s index unavailable. That is the trade, stated precisely.
A one-way door
“After a log group is created, its log class can’t be changed.”
Migration means a new log group — and every producer, IaC reference, dashboard and alarm that names it.
Also: a Delivery class exists only for Lambda logs bound for S3 or Firehose, fixed at two days and not queryable.
And the rename — inputs accept both names indefinitely, but from December 2026 reads return ESSENTIALS.
Essentials is for logs you want to have. Standard is for logs you want to act on.
Unsure? Standard. It is the only one of the two choices you are allowed to regret.
